newsitem.title: FRANCE: Euro-court upholds France on pharmacy complaint.
newsitem.headline: Euro-court upholds France on pharmacy complaint.

text.p: The European Court of Human Rights upheld on Friday a French law banning supermarkets from selling common pharmaceutical products such as vitamins and rubbing alcohol.

Reversing an earlier recommendation from the European Commission of Human Rights, the court concluded that French courts acted appropriately in convicting a supermarket manager in the central city of Sens for selling "medicinal products" reserved by law for pharmacies.
The courts had pursued manager Michel Cantoni after pharmacists in the area complained he was encroaching on their traditional turf.
The court acknowledged that the legal definition of medicinal products left grey areas but said French courts had consistently applied the law in the past in interpreting the definition.
Given the French courts' consistent rulings, manager Michel Cantoni "should have appreciated that...he ran a real risk of prosecution for unlawful sale of medicinal products," the court found.
The Human Rights Court and the Rights Commission are part of the Council of Europe, created after World War Two to foster democracy and human rights.
Britain's consumer watchdog decided last month to take legal action to end minimum prices on over-the-counter medicines that would allow supermarkets to undercut traditional pharmacies.
